front_blocks.md: Define **respiration**.

front_blocks.md: What is the difference between respiration and gas exchange?

back_blocks.md: **Gas exchange** gets oxygen into cells and carbon dioxide out.
**Respiration** then uses that oxygen to **release energy as ATP**.

It takes place in the **mitochondria**.

front_blocks.md: Define **anaerobic respiration**.

It is an **incomplete breakdown of glucose**, so it releases **less ATP**.

front_blocks.md: When does anaerobic respiration occur in animals?

back_blocks.md: Mainly in **muscle cells during vigorous exercise**, when the body cannot deliver enough **oxygen** to meet the muscles' higher demand for energy.

front_blocks.md: What problem does a build-up of lactic acid cause?

back_blocks.md: It **lowers the pH** of the muscle tissue, making conditions more acidic, which can **denature the enzymes** in cells.

front_blocks.md: Outline the limewater method for the carbon dioxide investigation.

back_blocks.md: Pour 2 cm<sup>3</sup> of **limewater** into three boiling tubes.
Set up three more tubes on damp cotton wool: **A** with germinating seeds, **B** with boiled seeds, **C** with glass beads.
Seal each seed tube with a bung and **delivery tube** into the limewater, with the end **submerged**.
Leave at **25–30 °C** for several hours, then observe any colour changes.

cards.front_md: Outline the limewater method for the carbon dioxide investigation.
cards.back_md:
Pour 2 cm<sup>3</sup> of **limewater** into three boiling tubes.

Set up three more tubes on damp cotton wool: **A** with germinating seeds, **B** with boiled seeds, **C** with glass beads.

Seal each seed tube with a bung and **delivery tube** into the limewater, with the end **submerged**.

Leave at **25–30 °C** for several hours, then observe any colour changes.

front_blocks.md: What happens to the limewater with germinating seeds, and why?

back_blocks.md: It turns **cloudy/milky**.
The germinating seeds are **respiring** and releasing **carbon dioxide**, which reacts with the limewater.

cards.front_md: What happens to the limewater with germinating seeds, and why?
cards.back_md:
It turns **cloudy/milky**.

front_blocks.md: Why are boiled seeds used as a control?

back_blocks.md: Boiled seeds are **dead**, so they do **not respire** and release no carbon dioxide — the limewater stays clear.

cards.front_md: Why are boiled seeds used as a control?
cards.back_md: Boiled seeds are **dead**, so they do **not respire** and release no carbon dioxide — the limewater stays clear.

front_blocks.md: Why are glass beads included in the carbon dioxide investigation?

back_blocks.md: As a **control for volume** — there is **no living material**, so no respiration and no carbon dioxide, and the limewater stays clear.

cards.front_md: Why are glass beads included in the carbon dioxide investigation?

front_blocks.md: Outline the vacuum flask method for the heat investigation.

back_blocks.md: **Sterilise** the seeds and flasks with weak bleach.
Set up **flask A** with dead seeds and **flask B** with germinating seeds, on moist cotton wool.
Insert a **thermometer** into each so the bulb sits among the seeds, and seal the tops with cotton wool.
**Invert** both flasks, record the **initial temperature**, then record the **final temperature** after 2–3 days.

cards.front_md: Outline the vacuum flask method for the heat investigation.
cards.back_md:
**Sterilise** the seeds and flasks with weak bleach.

Set up **flask A** with dead seeds and **flask B** with germinating seeds, on moist cotton wool.

Insert a **thermometer** into each so the bulb sits among the seeds, and seal the tops with cotton wool.

**Invert** both flasks, record the **initial temperature**, then record the **final temperature** after 2–3 days.

front_blocks.md: Why must the seeds and flasks be sterilised?

back_blocks.md: To **kill any microorganisms** present.
Otherwise **microbial decay** would raise the temperature in **both** flasks, rather than the respiring seeds.

front_blocks.md: What results are expected from the heat investigation?

back_blocks.md: The flask with **germinating seeds** shows a clear **temperature rise**, because respiration releases heat energy.
The flask with **dead seeds** shows **no change**, because they are not respiring.

cards.front_md: What results are expected from the heat investigation?

back_blocks.md: So that any temperature change in the **dead-seed control flask** can be attributed to a change in **room temperature**, not to respiration.
